notes.decision: Preserved as Coptic numeral '470' in title. May represent kephalaion-internal section number or a folio/quire mark; its exact function on this page is uncertain.

Translated 'the Five Vigils.' Parsed as ⲛ̄-ϯⲟⲩ-ⲣ̄ⲱⲉ where ⲣ̄ⲱⲉ is Lyc. for ⲣⲟⲉⲓⲥ 'wakefulness, vigil' (cf. ⲣ̄-ⲣⲟⲉⲓⲥ 'keep watch'). The disciplinary 'five watches' the teacher must establish. Cf. line 22 ⲛⲓⲁⲛⲟⲩⲣ̄ⲱⲉ 'the Watchers/Wakeful Ones,' which uses the same root cosmologically.
Translated 'leaps up.' Parsed as ⲱⲁ-ϥ-ϩⲉⲗ habitual + verb ϩⲱⲗ 'fly, leap' (cf. parallel ⲱⲁϩⲱⲧⲁⲣⲧⲣ̄ 'habitually disturbs' in next line). The subject is the disturbance/burdening that follows.

Translated 'the burdening of his mind.' ⲣ̄ⲫⲟⲣⲉ from Greek φορεῖν 'bear, wear, carry' (cf. ⲣ̄ⲫⲟⲣⲥ in glossary); nominalized: 'the bearing/burden.' The phrase parallels and is in apposition with ⲛ̄ϩⲱⲧⲁⲣⲧⲣ̄ 'disturbance.'

Translated 'his master.' ⲥⲁϩ = 'master, scribe, teacher'; here distinguished from ⲣⲉϩ†ⲥⲃⲱ ('teacher') in the immediately following line, indicating a doublet 'master and teacher' for the apostle/instructor relation.

Translated 'before him.' Lyc. ⲛⲁϩⲣⲉϥ — preposition 'in the presence of him.' Functions to introduce the list of those 'before him' who become enemies (line 8 closes the inclusio with the same ⲛⲁⲍⲣⲉϩ).
Translated 'they become as enemies.' ⲱⲁⲩⲣ̄ = habitual + ⲣ̄- 'do/become'; ⲧⲍⲉ = ⲧ-ϩⲉ 'the manner of'; ⲛⲓⲝⲁⲝⲉ = ⲛⲓϫⲁϫⲉ 'the enemies.' Literally 'they become the manner of enemies.'

Translated 'arise away from his hand.' ⲡⲧⲱⲛⲉ = nominalized ⲧⲱⲟⲩⲛ 'rise, depart'; the love and desire 'depart from his hand,' i.e. leave his possession. Same root verb appears at line 16 'depart on a journey.'

Translated 'the part separated forth.' ⲡⲁⲥⲉ = Lyc. ⲡⲁϣ 'half, division, portion'; ⲡⲱⲣⲝ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'separate forth' (= ⲡⲱⲣϫ in vocab). The fallen man becomes a vessel of the schism/separation from the Church.

Translated 'he is filled instead by the evil spirit.' ⲍⲁ = Lyc. ϩⲁ 'under, by, instead of'; with the agentive sense 'is filled by/under (the influence of).' ⲡⲛⲁ ⲉⲧⲍⲁⲩ = 'the evil spirit' (cf. ϩⲟⲟⲩ/ⲍⲁⲩ in glossary).
Translated 'they fall.' Conjunctive ⲛ̄ⲥⲉ- + ⲉⲓⲣⲉ ⲛ-ϩⲉ or ⲣ̄-ϩⲉ — possibly 'do a fall' = 'fall' (ϩⲉ 'fall'). Subject is the evil spirits/error-powers who fall upon the disturbed teacher.
Translated 'in the flight of a bird.' ⲣ̄ⲫⲉ tentatively a verbal noun on ⲡⲏⲧ/ⲡⲱⲧ 'flee, fly' (Lyc. ⲡ→ⲫ regular). The simile compares disturbed cosmic men to migratory birds drawn far away.
Translated 'as foreigners.' Parsed as ⲛ-ⲟⲩ-ⲣ̄-ⲣⲁⲙⲛⲕⲁⲍ 'of becoming/being foreigners' or simply ⲛ-ⲣⲙⲛⲕⲁⲍ 'of strangers/of those who belong to a (foreign) land.' Cf. ⲣⲙⲛⲕⲁⲍ in glossary.
Translated 'I have made you see.' Idiomatic 'open your eye(s) forth' = reveal/make to see. ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩ-ⲉⲓⲁⲧ⸗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ is the standard Coptic causative-revelation idiom.

Translated 'the matter.' ⲡⲱⲓ = 'that which belongs to'; ⲡⲍⲱϩ ambiguously could be ⲡϩⲱⲃ 'the work/matter' (cf. ⲡⲍⲱⲃ in glossary) or ⲡϩⲟ 'the face' or a possessive form. 'The matter' (= the bodily/cosmic structure they have shrunk into) fits the parallel with ⲥⲱⲙⲁ in line 29.

Translated 'lofty ... bent down.' ϩⲝⲁⲥⲉ = ϫⲁⲥⲉ 'lofty, high' (qualitative); ⲁϩⲕⲁⲗⲉⲝ probably ⲁϥ-ⲕⲱⲗϫ 'he bent (himself) down' — preserving the spatial-vertical contrast with the preceding 'great and high.'
Translated 'they are gathered.' Likely Lyc. qualitative of ⲥⲱⲟⲩϩ 'gather, assemble.' The Watchers in the Zone are gathered/concentrated in their proper station.

Translated 'they are not defiled.' ϫⲱϩⲙ̄ 'defile, pollute'; with negative ⲉⲛ. The Watchers, though constrained in the Zone, remain pure — paralleling the Mind of Light's preservation despite bodily contraction.
